C-BROWSER-M1-1-AUDIT-CLOSURE-HARDENING-2.Title: Browser M1.1 Audit Closure Hardening: Kernel Event Transport Publication, Exact Context Scope Validation, Targeted ElementRef Action Addressing and CI Fail-Closed Policy
C-BROWSER-M1-1-AUDIT-CLOSURE-HARDENING-2.Summary: Finalize and close Milestone M1.1 audit findings: 1. Replace local Vec event accumulation in browser provider with genuine M0.4 kernel event transport publication via InvocationContext::publish_event, verified by authorized pull subscriptions receiving EventEnvelope. 2. Eliminate the string-prefix loophole in provider resource scope checking; require exact resource matches or validated parent context ownership. 3. Wire ElementRef.node_key directly to specific DOM/AX elements in the real Chromium executor so actions address targeted elements rather than generic document.querySelector('input')/'button'. 4. Make real Chromium acceptance test fail-closed in CI environments when the browser binary cannot be spawned.

Goals.Goal: Publish browser events directly through InvocationContext::publish_event to M0.4 kernel event transport.
Ensure authorized kernel event subscribers receive real EventEnvelopes from browser capability operations.
Eliminate string-prefix bypass in check_resource_scope by requiring exact match or validated owning context.
Target specific DOM elements in Chromium executor by ElementRef.node_key.
Enforce fail-closed browser detection in CI runner environments.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Full production CEF embedding in M1.1 (reserved for M1.2 based on this spike's measurements).
Public internet network crawling or remote web page dependencies.

Constraints.Constraint: BROWSER EVENTS MUST BE PUBLISHED VIA INVOCATIONCONTEXT AND RECEIVED VIA KERNEL EVENT TRANSPORT.
RESOURCE SCOPE VALIDATION MUST NOT ALLOW ARBITRARY PREFIX BYPASSES.
CHROMIUM ACTION EXECUTION MUST RESOLVE SPECIFIC TARGETED ELEMENTREF NODES.
REAL ENGINE ACCEPTANCE TEST MUST FAIL CLOSED IN CI ENVIRONMENTS.
KERNEL REMAINS 100% ENGINE-NEUTRAL AND IMPORTS ZERO BROWSER TYPES.

C-BROWSER-M1-1-AUDIT-CLOSURE-HARDENING-2.VerificationIntent: Verify that browser events are received by authorized kernel event subscribers as real EventEnvelopes. Verify that arbitrary context grants cannot access unowned pages. Verify that ElementRef.node_key targets specific interactive DOM elements in real Chromium. Verify that real Chromium acceptance test fails closed in CI if browser is missing.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Browser events (page.created, navigation.committed, page.closed, download.started) are published via kernel transport and received by SubscriptionHandle.
check_resource_scope strictly rejects cross-context page access and unauthorized context scopes.
Real Chromium action execution targets the specific element referenced by ElementRef.node_key.
real_chromium_acceptance fails closed in CI environment if browser cannot be spawned.
All CI suites (Source, Correctness, ArchitectureSecurity, ProvingSlice, All) pass cleanly.
